habitat: Wherever a small win needs an oversized reaction: comment sections, sports highlights, personal milestones.
diet: Feeds on disproportion — a minor victory rendered at maximum emotional intensity.
predators: Statutory damages. Griner v. King for Congress (2024, affirmed on appeal, cert denied 2025) is this specimen's own predator, on the public record.
transmission: Almost entirely as the unaltered photograph; the format resists redrawing because the expression is the content.
cause_of_death: None recorded. The specimen has not gone extinct — it has gone corporate.
resurrection: Not applicable. It never stopped circulating; the rights holder redirected the circulation rather than ending it.
host_population: General, skewing toward any personal or minor triumph worth captioning.
mutation: Minimal. Unlike a drawn species, a photographic specimen mutates by caption only, never by redrawing.
prognosis: The meme is in no danger. Anyone using it commercially without a licence is. See merch_posture.
minor_in_image: Yes (11 months at time of photo)
enforcement_history: Griner v. King for Congress. Jury found infringement, awarded $750 statutory minimum. Eighth Circuit affirmed June 2024, rejecting fair use under Warhol. Supreme Court denied certiorari January 2025.
curatorial_note: Owner licenses to major brands and has said she objects to commercial use she has not approved. Subject was an infant, so likeness rights sit alongside copyright.
